subject: Production throughput collapse after v4.2-q3 deployment — urgent
messages:
From: Stephanie Hart <stephanie.hart@acme-retail.com>
To: support@redwood.ai; soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: throughput collapse & 502s after model v4.2-q3 deploy

Team —

We pushed the new model artifact (v4.2) with the q3 quantization profile to production at 02:30 PT last night and immediately observed a steep drop in sustained throughput for our checkout inference path. Metrics summary attached (acme_prod_logs_20280524.zip):
- Throughput up to 70% lower on typical 99th percentile traffic windows.
- P99 latency increased from ~320ms to ~780ms for the same request mix.
- 502/5xx errors spiked from 0.1% to 3.6% across multiple regions — customers are seeing timeouts/failures.
- Elevated decode stalls seen in token-level traces (attached p99_traces.html).

This is impacting order completion. We rolled back on our side at ~06:00 PT and saw some recovery, but we need Redwood to confirm root cause and a remediation plan. We require one of the following ASAP:
1) Immediate rollback of the v4.2-q3 variant for Acme on your side if it's still routed to some capacity pools;
2) Hotfix guidance we can apply (config flags, routing adjustments) and a target time to full recovery;
3) If a configuration change is required on Redwood, we need an explicit timeline and an SLA credit proposal.

I've attached the logs and traces. Procurement copied for visibility — this is on the path to an SLA breach.

-Stephanie Hart
SRE Lead, Production Engineering
Acme Retail

Attachments: acme_prod_logs_20280524.zip, p99_traces.html

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie.hart@acme-retail.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: throughput collapse & 502s after model v4.2-q3 deploy

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. We're pulling a hot team onto this now. Immediate steps:
- I'm opening an incident and assigning Karthik (engineer) + Irene (runtime) to triage the kernel/quant interactions.
- Can you confirm whether any traffic is still routed to v4.2-q3 from your side? You mentioned you rolled back at ~06:00 PT, but we want to ensure no drift in routing/edge caches.
- We'll validate whether we still have any warm nodes running v4.2-q3 and prepare an emergency rollback if needed.

Tentative timeline: 30m for quick triage and an ops call at 09:55 PT to decide on rollback vs. config patch. Marissa, I'm looping you for customer comms and credits discussion.

From: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai; irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie.hart@acme-retail.com; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: throughput collapse & 502s after model v4.2-q3 deploy

Quick initial findings from a 15m run against the provided traces and our infra telemetry:
- The v4.2 architecture + q3 profile triggers a different kernel selection path on our accelerated runtime. That path increases KV-cache eviction frequency for long-context checkout sessions.
- Increased cache churn correlates with token decode stalls and a jump in retry/queueing at the serving layer — explains both p99 latency jump and 502s under burst.
- We also see a subtle change in memory working set that increases GC/host-side stalls on certain GPU SKUs; this shows up in the traces as short-lived service hiccups.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
A) Pin Acme's routing to the previous variant (v4.1-q2) and route requests off any nodes still running v4.2-q3. This is fastest and reverses behavior.
B) Disable continuous batching on Acme's high-QPS routes for 2h to avoid cache churn while we push a qprofile tweak.
C) If rollback is not permitted, deploy a temporary kernel flag to force the earlier kernel selection (we can ship this in ~2–3h).

I recommend A + B to stop the customer impact now, then C for a more stable rollout. I'm starting a rollback runbook and will coordinate with Soojin for approvals.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; irene_choi@redwood.ai; procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: throughput collapse & 502s after model v4.2-q3 deploy — customer escalation & next steps

Stephanie — I'm really sorry for the disruption. I'm Marissa, the account lead for Acme. Quick summary and asks so we can align with your execs:
- Redwood action: engineering recommends rolling Acme back to v4.1-q2 immediately and disabling continuous batching for the critical checkout route while we push a qprofile fix.
- Customer impact: we understand this is affecting checkout conversions and may trigger SLA credit clauses. I'm prepared to offer a proactive credit while we remediate — my proposed starting point is a 2-month credit against inference usage while the RCA and final fix are delivered.
- Next steps: approve the rollback (if you haven't already) and join an incident review call at 11:00 PT today so we can confirm timelines and comms.

If we need additional executive escalation we can loop our CSM/CS leadership. What's the best number to reach you for the call?

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; soojin_lee@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; stephanie.hart@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 25 May 2028 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: throughput collapse & 502s after model v4.2-q3 deploy — rollback status

Update from the ERT call and actions taken:
- We initiated a rollback of Acme traffic to v4.1-q2 at 13:12 PT (25 May). Traffic switch completed at 13:18 PT.
- Within 20 minutes we're seeing error rate fall from 3.6% -> 0.2% and p99 latency move from ~780ms -> ~340ms (monitoring dashboards refreshed).
- We captured additional token-level traces post-rollback; the working hypothesis (per Karthik) is quant-profile interaction with kernel selection + cache churn.
- Next steps: 1) schedule a 72-hour controlled re-roll with an adjusted qprofile and kernel-flag guardrails; 2) produce an RCA doc by EOD Friday with root cause and mitigation checklist; 3) propose a product change to make qprofile-to-kernel mappings explicit in the model catalog to avoid silent kernel-path changes.

I've attached the p99_traces.html that compares pre/post rollback for the incident.

Thanks — Irene
VP, Serving Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

(on-call runbook: https://redwood.app/drive/teams/ops/acme-inc/incident-ACME-42)
